data.title: Meduza: Remembering Marina Vlady, the cinema icon who embodied the ‘mysterious Russian soul’ for Europeans. To Soviet audiences, she was an enigmatic French star — and bard Vladimir Vysotsky’s muse.
data.summary: French actress Marina Vlady died on September 24 at 88. Born outside Paris to a Russian émigré family, she often played women with a “mysterious Russian soul” in European films — perhaps because of her background. Soviet audiences first knew her as the enigmatic witch in André Michel’s melodrama “The Blonde Witch,” and only later as Vladimir Vysotsky’s muse and wife. She appeared in numerous Italian films, including films with Marcello Mastroianni, and won the Best Actress award at the 1963 Cannes Film Festival for “A Modern Story: The Queen Bee.” Film critic Anton Dolin looks back on an actress whose story extends far beyond one famous romance.

data.title: Meduza: One in three members of Russia’s new State Duma has ties to the war in Ukraine. Some are accused of war crimes. Here’s who they are — and what they’ve done.
data.summary: Russia has held its first State Duma elections since the start of the full-scale war. According to preliminary results, United Russia has won a record number of seats — more than three-quarters of the chamber. The party has already said that 49 “participants in the special military operation” will become lawmakers on its ticket, effectively answering Putin’s call for military personnel to become Russia’s “new elite.” But they make up only part of what might be called the Duma’s “war faction.” Many incoming lawmakers who have never fought on the front are nonetheless involved in the war, whether by financing it or providing infrastructure to support it. Meduza examined the backgrounds of everyone projected to enter parliament based on the preliminary results. By our count, the “war faction” consists of 148 lawmakers — a third of the State Duma. And that includes only those with clear ties to the war that can be traced through open sources.
